analysis:
This batch has two files with no executable behavior change. deploy/provider-fleet/update-fleet.sh changes only header comments (lines 8-12). It now says the dev installer writes the dev coordinator URL into ~/.config/darkbloom/provider.toml, and the prod installer leaves it unchanged. The executable logic is identical to base: the --force-prod guard, the fixed COORD_URL values, and the ssh invocation of `curl -fsSL $COORD_URL/install.sh | bash`. No new attack surface appears in this file. docs/developer/test.md changes only the date and adds test documentation. That text covers scripts/test-install-coordinator-binding.py, InstallerCoordinatorBindingTests, TestServedInstallerBindsProviderToServingCoordinator, and `go test ./coordinator/cmd/devnet-seed`, which needs a disposable DATABASE_URL and refuses a database that already has users. This documents safe-handling practice and weakens no mitigation.

Cross-file note: the described installer behavior of rewriting the `[coordinator] url` line in provider.toml lives in install.sh and the coordinator-served installer, not in this batch. A later pass should check those files for whether the URL is bound to the serving coordinator only, whether the dev-to-prod and prod-to-dev directions are correct, and whether the config write can redirect a provider to an attacker-controlled coordinator. That relates to TB-002 and T-040 (Host-header-derived installer URLs). The existing curl|bash over ssh pattern is pre-existing and not new here. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by these two files.
